Its work includes detecting epidemic threats, sequencing and identifying pathogens, and supporting rapid action to protect communities.

stories.headline: Delhi High Court Directs Authorities To Provide Industrialist Anil Ambani's Son Details Of LOC Against Him
stories.title: Delhi High Court Directs Authorities To Provide Industrialist Anil Ambani's Son Details Of LOC Against Him
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Delhi High Court has directed the authorities to provide Jai Anshul Anil Ambani, son of industrialist Anil Ambani, specific details of the Look Out Circular (LOC) issued against him, including the date of its issuance, and a copy of the formal order.
Justice Mini Pushkarna passed the direction while hearing an application filed by Jai Anshul seeking compliance of an earlier order passed on September 17 by a coordinate bench.

The Court was informed that the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) had communicated to Jai Anshul on October 05 that an LOC had been issued against him in view of an ongoing investigation and that it continued to remain in force.
However, his counsel submitted that the communication was vague and did not disclose specific details regarding the LOC.
Taking note of the communication, the Court directed the authorities to provide details regarding when the LOC was issued and furnish a copy of the formal order to Jai Anshul in accordance with law.
The Court also took note of Ambani's submission that the communication was received only from the SFIO and not from the Bureau of Immigration.

“Accordingly, respondents are further directed to apprise the Court as to whether any other LOC has been issued against the petitioner, which is in the knowledge of the Bureau of Immigration,” the Court said.

During the hearing, counsel for the authorities submitted that the earlier direction had required the petition to be treated as a representation and requisite intimation to be provided within a time-bound manner.
It was argued that the Court had not directed the authorities to furnish specific details of the LOC.
The respondents also submitted that if Jai Anshul was dissatisfied with the communication issued by the SFIO, he could pursue other remedies available to him.
The matter will be considered next on October 16.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice To Union, ECI On ADR's Plea Challenging Lifelong Immunity To CEC, Election Commissioners
stories.title: Supreme Court Issues Notice To Union, ECI On ADR's Plea Challenging Lifelong Immunity To CEC, Election Commissioners
stories.summary: The plea seeks revival of proceedings against current and past CEC/Election Commissioners.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The plea seeks revival of proceedings against current and past CEC/Election Commissioners.

The Supreme Court today issued notice on a petition filed by the Association for Democratic Reforms challenging the immunity granted to Chief Election Commissioner/Election Commissioners for actions taken in purported discharge of official duties.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana sought the response of the Union and the Election Commission on ADR's challenge to the constitutional validity of Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.
Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan appeared for ADR.
The petition has been filed through AoR Rani Mishra.
Briefly put, the petition seeks a declaration that Section 16 of the CEC Act is unconstitutional, void and inoperative as violative of Articles 14 and 21 and the basic structure of the Constitution.
It further seeks revival of proceedings against the present and past CEC and Election Commissioners, which came to an end as Section 16 of the CEC Act came into effect.

"Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, no Court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings against any person who is or was a Chief Election Commissioner or an Election Commissioner for any act, thing or word, committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty or function."
The petition contends that Section 16 provides blanket immunity to the current and previous CEC/ECs for lifetime, which has no rational nexus with the objective of ensuring independence of CEC/ECs.
The provision places the CEC & ECs beyond the reach of any Court of law, it highlights.
"No other provision in the Constitution of India or any statute grants immunity that is at once lifelong, unconditioned by good faith, free of any sanction mechanism, and without a saving clause."
Petitioner-ADR further points out that Section 16 was not originally part of the Bill introduced.

Opposition parties, including the Congress, have alleged that eligible voters are being excluded and the process favoured the ruling BJP.
Not only did the poll body deny these allegations, Kumar also challenged Rahul Gandhi to substantiate his allegations of vote theft or apologise.
After criticism over the deletion of around 13 crore voters, the ECI ordered a special enrolment drive for voters left out during the SIR process.

article_sentences: Congress workers staged a protest rally in Hubballi on October 11, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of electoral malpractice and attempts to undermine democracy.

The rally was organised by the Vidyanagar and Unkal block Congress committees under the leadership of Rajat Ullagaddimath, Chairperson of the Hubballi-Dharwad City District Guarantee Schemes Implementation Authority.
It began at Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Circle, where the protesters read out Article 326 of the Constitution, which provides for elections based on adult suffrage.
Addressing the gathering, Mr. Ullagaddimath alleged that the RSS is conspiring to deprive oppressed and marginalised communities of their right to vote.
Describing the struggle to protect democracy and the Constitution as a ‘second freedom struggle’ against what he termed fascist forces, he called for concerted action to safeguard electoral rights.

Hundreds of Congress workers accused the BJP-led Union Government of attempting to manipulate the votes of Other Backward Classes, Economically Weaker Sections, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and minority communities.
They raised slogans against the Centre and demanded Mr. Kumar’s resignation.
Tension prevailed when the rally reached the Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation office.
Protesters allegedly attempted to burn portraits of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and Mr. Kumar, triggering a scuffle between the police and the demonstrators.
The police, subsequently, detained several protesters.

Hubballi-Dharwad District Congress president Sadanand Danganavar, I.G. Sanadi, KPCC member Satish Meharwade, Shahzaman Mujahid, Anwar Mudgol, Mohammed Sharif Gargad, and several councillors and party functionaries participated in the protest.

stories.title: Kerala Congress Faces BJP Attack Over SIR After UDF’s Election Victory

article_sentences: Kerala’s Congress-led UDF government faces BJP criticism after the state Assembly passed a resolution seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal and questioning the voter-roll revision exercise that preceded its election victory.

The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government in Kerala has come under fire from the BJP after the state Assembly passed a resolution questioning the Election Commission of India’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The resolution has sparked a political controversy because the UDF swept to power in the Assembly elections in May, months after the voter-roll revision was completed.
The BJP has accused the Congress of contradicting itself by challenging the credibility of an electoral process that preceded its victory.
The controversy has also drawn attention to remarks by senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor, who had suggested that the SIR exercise might have benefited the party in Kerala.
On Monday, the Kerala Assembly passed the resolution with 137 of its 140 members voting in its favour.
The three BJP MLAs opposed the bill, which is said to be the first of its kind in the nation.

The resolution demands the removal of Chief Minister VD Satheesan, restoration of names of eligible voters whose names were deleted in the SIR exercise and changes in the appointment process of the election commissioners, the Chief Minister said.

Satheesan however said that the matter needed to be discussed as there were some concerns about the roll revision procedure, the potential exclusion of eligible citizens and the neutrality of the Election Commission.
In a post on X, he said the integrity of the electoral process was non-negotiable and described the right to vote as a foundation of democracy.
The resolution aligns with the Congress’s broader national campaign against the SIR process and its demand for action against the Chief Election Commissioner.
Kerala was included in the second phase of the nationwide SIR exercise announced on October 27, 2025, alongside Assam, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry.

stories.headline: SC questions Delhi Police over alleged assault on women journalists
stories.title: SC questions Delhi Police over alleged assault on women journalists
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 13 : The Supreme Court on Tuesday took serious note of allegations that women journalists covering protests in the national capital were assaulted by police personnel and directed a senior Delhi Police officer to remain present during the hearing on Thursday to explain the matter. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana made the observation after senior advocate Indira Jaising mentioned a petition filed by the Network of Women in Media, India (NWMI), seeking safeguards for journalists covering protests, particularly women journalists. "We would like some senior officer to remain present here and explain," the CJI Kant-led Bench said, indicating that the police would have to explain the allegations. The development comes amid allegations that journalists covering protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar were manhandled, detained and obstructed while discharging their professional duties on October 10 and 11. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan also mentioned a separate contempt petition alleging that the police had assaulted journalists in violation of the Supreme Court’s October 10 order. The apex court had directed the authorities to ensure that lawyers, journalists and other professionals were not hindered in discharging their professional duties. The directions were passed by a Bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana while hearing contempt petitions alleging violations of its order concerning restrictions imposed ahead of the proposed protest. It had also directed the authorities to ensure the normal functioning of Metro and railway services, uninterrupted internet connectivity and free movement of people, subject to traffic regulations and public order requirements. The Supreme Court had also directed that there should be no detention except in accordance with the procedure established by law, particularly in the case of peaceful and unarmed gatherings outside areas where prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were in force. --IANS

stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 13 : The Reserve Bank of India is likely to stay on tightening path through H1FY28 and may hike the repo rate by around 75 basis points, according to leading brokerages. According to the NDTV Profit report, global brokerages -- including BofA, Goldman Sachs and UBS -- said that the Middle East tensions, energy supply disruptions and intensifying El Nino could push headline CPI higher. BofA and UBS have forecast that the central bank will tighten monetary policy and expect around a 75-basis-point repo rate hike in MPC meetings scheduled for FY27, extending up to the first half of fiscal 2028. Apart from that, UBS predicted full-year headline inflation to average near 5.2 per cent in FY27, while it could cross 5 per cent through first half of FY28 due to adverse weather-related strains. "As per our global strategy team, historical evidence suggests that effects typically materialize with a lag of 6-18 months following peak weather disruption. With likely peak occurring between November and February, most significant impact on global food prices may emerge during 2027 and early 2028, adding upside risks to inflation outlook," the brokerage forecasted. Additionally, they flagged upside risks after India's consumer inflation touched a 23-month high in September on surge in food prices. The report highlighted that headline Consumer Price Index inflation came at 5.54 per cent in September, up from 4.8 per cent in August, driven largely by higher food and vegetable prices. Moreover, food inflation climbed to 7.74 per cent in September from 5.97 per cent in August, while food and beverages inflation rose to 7.36 per cent from 5.66 per cent. Notably, rise in inflation was more pronounced in rural areas, where consumer inflation stood at 6.08 per cent in September, compared with 4.88 per cent in urban areas. CPI (General) index for combined category increased to 109.49 in September from 108.74 in August. Similarly, combined CFPI index rose to 112.17 from 110.73 during same period. --IANS

stories.headline: US Democrats’ House victory could test Trump’s India policy
stories.title: US Democrats’ House victory could test Trump’s India policy
stories.summary: Washington, Oct 13 : Democrats are heavy favourites to win control of the US House of Representatives in the November 3 midterm elections, according to the prediction markets and polling averages, raising the prospect of tougher congressional scrutiny of President Donald Trump's tariff, trade and visa policies that weigh heavily on India. Traders on the prediction market Kalshi gave Democrats a 90 per cent chance of taking the House and a 62 per cent chance of winning the Senate, according to prices published on Monday. Kalshi put the chance of a Democratic sweep of both chambers at 61 per cent. The next most likely outcome, at 30 per cent, was a divided Congress with Democrats running the House and Republicans keeping the Senate. The Silver Bulletin polling average, updated on Monday, had Democrats ahead by 8.8 points on the generic congressional ballot, which asks voters which party they will support for Congress. "Democrats' surge in the polls that started in early September still hasn't stopped," the Silver Bulletin said. Trump's own numbers offer his party little cover. A CBS News/YouGov poll conducted from September 30 to October 2 found 39 per cent of Americans approved of his job performance and 61 per cent disapproved. On inflation, only 29 per cent approved and 71 per cent disapproved. The Senate is far less certain. The Cook Political Report rates seven races as toss-ups: Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas. Six of those seats are held by Republicans. A Democratic House would give the party subpoena power and committee gavels. House Democrats are preparing "a vast oversight agenda" covering Trump, his family and his administration, US media said. London-based think tank Chatham House said Democrats' real leverage would be on money, even if they took only the House. The US debt limit is expected to be reached by mid-2027, and a Democratic House alone would rule out Republicans using the budget reconciliation process to raise it, Max Yoeli, a senior research fellow at Chatham House, wrote last month. Yoeli also cautioned that opposition on foreign policy "will be more about optics than hard constraints", since Democrats would lack the votes to override presidential vetoes. For India, that points to a Democratic House making its mark mostly through oversight rather than new law. Trump's tariffs have largely been imposed through executive action. A Democratic House could hold hearings and force votes on them, but would struggle to overturn them against a veto. The same applies to the Graham Act tariffs on top buyers of Russian energy, which could take effect from October 18. The law requires the administration to send Congress a written justification at least 10 days before imposing such duties, a requirement that a Democratic-led House would be well placed to press. Any India-US trade agreement that needs legislation would also face a more sceptical chamber. The $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions, which falls heavily on Indian professionals, is already tied up in court. A federal judge in California blocked its enforcement on September 30, and the administration has appealed to the Ninth Circuit. Democrats could add hearings and spending riders to that legal fight. Indian nationals have historically accounted for the largest share of H-1B beneficiaries. The four Indian-American members seeking re-election to the House, Ro Khanna, Ami Bera, Pramila Jayapal and Suhas Subramanyam, all Democrats, are in races rated safe for their party. The current House has six Indian-American members. Raja Krishnamoorthi gave up his seat to run for the Senate and lost the Illinois primary, while Shri Thanedar lost his Michigan primary in August. The House has 435 voting members, and a party needs 218 seats for a majority. All House seats and 35 Senate seats are on the ballot on November 3. --IANS

stories.summary: Mumbai, Oct 13 : BJP leader and former MP Kirit Somaiya has approached the Union Ministry of Home Affairs and immigration authorities, urging them to issue a Look Out Circular (LOC) against actor Imran Khan. He has also requested that the actor be barred from leaving the country until an inquiry into his complaint and the investigation into a Mumbai police case are completed. In a letter dated October 13 to Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Somaiya called on the Ministry of Home Affairs to issue directions preventing Khan from travelling abroad under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025. He also asked the Bureau of Immigration to issue an LOC against the actor and notify the police should he attempt to leave India. The move comes after a protest at Mumbai’s August Kranti Maidan on October 10 where demonstrators demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. In his letter, Somaiya claimed that the gathering had taken place without the necessary permission. He further alleged that Khan had attended and participated in the protest before Mumbai Police detained him at the venue. According to the letter, Gamdevi Police Station registered an FIR, numbered 813 of 2026, in connection with the incident, with Khan named in the case. Somaiya also stated that he had not received a copy of the FIR. Somaiya claimed in his letter that Khan is a US citizen and reportedly holds an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card. He urged the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Bureau of Immigration to assess whether the actor’s participation in the protest calls for action under Section 7D of the Citizenship Act, 1955, and the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025. Somaiya also took to X to share a copy of the letter addressed to the Union Home Secretary, detailing his request for a Look Out Circular against actor Imran Khan. Sharing the same, he wrote, “Requested Immigration Home Ministry to issue a LOC ( look out circular) against #ImranKhan to NOT to leave India.” Somaiya has further urged the Bureau of Immigration to alert Gamdevi Police Station if Khan attempts to travel outside India. He has also sought a written update from the concerned authorities on the steps taken in response to his request. Actor Imran Khan was detained by Mumbai Police on October 10 while attending a demonstration at August Kranti Maidan. He had joined a protest organized by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), which called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. --IANS

Justice Bagchi replied, "you're right, but so can't High Court".

stories.title: Tamil Nadu’s claim of Cauvery backlog and the Supreme Court’s response | Explained
stories.summary: The failure of the southwest monsoon (June-September) this year is the primary reason for the current round of disputes between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The story so far: On October 12, the Supreme Court questioned Tamil Nadu on how Karnataka could be expected to make good the backlog in the release of Cauvery water when the latter was itself grappling with water scarcity and drought conditions.

A Division Bench of the Court made this observation while reserving its order on an application filed by Tamil Nadu, which contended that as on October 6, it suffered a shortfall of around 11.7 thousand million cubic feet (tmc ft) in realisation of its share of the Cauvery water at Biligundulu, the inter-State border measuring point.
What has caused the present situation?
The failure of the southwest monsoon (June-September) this year is the primary reason for the current round of disputes between the upper riparian and lower riparian States.
During the period from June 1 to October 7, the Cauvery catchments recorded a negative departure of 30% from the normal rainfall.
In particular, the deficit rainfall in the catchment downstream of Krishnaraja Sagara (KRS) and Kabini, up to Biligundulu, was 43%.
Against the quantity of 57.568 tmc ft to be realised during the corresponding period in such circumstances, the realisation was 45.849 tmc ft.

This was the figure worked out by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC), the main arm that assists the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA), the implementation mechanism for the final award of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal, as modified by the Supreme Court.
Tamil Nadu had, too, in its latest application, cited the figure of the CWRC.
In fact, at the Authority’s last meeting on October 8, the State demanded that a backlog of 15.02 tmc ft be made good by Karnataka.
How has Karnataka reacted to this demand?
Karnataka stated in the Supreme Court its difficulties in clearing the backlog.

stories.headline: Karnataka’s 56% quota falls in court: Will the Supreme Court revive the SC/ST hike?
stories.title: Karnataka’s 56% quota falls in court: Will the Supreme Court revive the SC/ST hike?
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Karnataka’s 56% reservation quota has been struck down by the High Court.
The state government plans to explore a Supreme Court appeal and has renewed its demand for a review of the 50% reservation ceiling.

Bengaluru: The Karnataka High Court has struck down the state’s decision to increase reservations for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes beyond the 50% ceiling, ruling the enhanced quota unconstitutional.
The 2022 legislation increased reservation for Scheduled Castes from 15% to 17% and for Scheduled Tribes from 3% to 7%.
This took the overall reservation in Karnataka for education and government jobs to 56%.
Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara said the state government would pursue all available legal options, including filing an appeal before the Supreme Court.

In a statement issued on Monday evening, Parameshwara urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Union government to undertake a comprehensive review of the 50% reservation ceiling and consider constitutional and legislative measures to address Karnataka’s demand.
He also called on the Centre to reconsider the state’s request to include the enhanced reservation provisions in the Constitution’s Ninth Schedule.
Parameshwara said the BJP government, which enacted the legislation in October 2022, was aware that the changes would raise the overall reservation quota to 56%.
He argued that the legislation was passed without securing the requested Ninth Schedule protection, despite the issue having been recognised by the government at the time.

According to Parameshwara, the Centre informed Parliament on July 25, 2026, that Karnataka’s proposal for inclusion in the Ninth Schedule had been deferred because the matter was pending before the High Court.
Former chief minister Siddaramaiah also called on the Union government to explain how it intended to address the issue.

stories.headline: Delhi to host first-ever BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ meeting today
stories.title: Delhi to host first-ever BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ meeting today
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 13 : India is set to host the first-ever BIMSTEC Home Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi on Tuesday, marking a significant step towards strengthening regional cooperation on security-related issues. Union Home Minister Amit Shah will chair the meeting. Describing the gathering as a historic occasion, HM Shah on Monday said the meeting underscores "our shared resolve to combat terrorism, transnational organised crime, narcotics radicalisation, trafficking, illicit financial flows, and cyber threats". "Through decisive coordination, we remain committed to building a safer, stronger, and more secure BIMSTEC," the Home Minister said. Officials from the member countries are expected to participate in the meeting. The meeting is expected to provide a platform for BIMSTEC member nations to discuss common security concerns and explore ways to enhance cooperation in addressing threats that extend across national borders. The gathering also highlights the importance of coordinated regional efforts to counter terrorism, organised criminal networks, drug-related threats, human trafficking and cybercrime. BIMSTEC, an acronym for the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation, is a regional organisation comprising seven member countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. According to the organisation's official website, BIMSTEC works to strengthen collaboration in areas such as agriculture and food security, the blue economy, connectivity, culture, disaster management, energy, environment and climate change, fiscal and monetary policy, health, human resource development, fisheries and livestock, and people-to-people relations, among other fields. In July this year, the 5th Meeting of the BIMSTEC National Security Chiefs was held in New Delhi, where the National Security Advisers and heads of delegations exchanged views on various measures to combat terrorism and organised crime; ensure security in the cyber, maritime and energy domains; enhance connectivity; facilitate efficient disaster management; and tackle new and emerging security threats. The meeting adopted the BIMSTEC Guidelines for the Maritime Component of Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief. The guidelines will help BIMSTEC member states undertake relief operations in the region in an expeditious manner. They also endorsed a set of Guiding Principles on the Conduct of Maritime Law Enforcement Agencies during Interactions at Sea. These principles are expected to provide reference points for increasing predictability and promoting safety during maritime engagements among member states. --IANS

Senior counsel Sacchin Puri mentioned the petitions before a bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma, asserting that protests have to be in a manner that does not hamper the professional work of lawyer and business of traders. "Traders have lost up to Rs 2,000 crore in recent times because of barricading and how protests are happening...People can't approach areas like Connaught Place. It is completely in approachable," Puri submitted. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma said the issues are substantively already pending before the Supreme Court. Agreeing to list the matter, the bench directed that the cases be taken up at the end of the board on Tuesday. Central Delhi has been witnessing massive protests by various opposition parties, student groups and civil society members over various issues.
